correctness.rationale: An exact iff criterion tests whether each of the 1767 minimum dominating eight-sets ceases to dominate after deletion. The 24-vertex, 36-edge graph is independently identified with a standard LCF model. Exhaustive finite enumerations check all 346104 seven-vertex candidates (zero dominating), all 735471 eight-vertex candidates (1767 dominating), every edge deletion size 0 through 5, and the 48 symmetry maps; a separate Python bitset implementation independently returns 276 and the same eight orbit sizes. No finite-to-infinite inference is used.

originality.rationale: The published September 2026 theorem fixes the minimum bondage size at five, but an existential witness and exhaustive four-edge lower bound do not specify the count of all 376992 candidate five-edge sets or their eight symmetry orbits. Relevant mathematical records and web searches were compared by logical strength and object. The closest relevant primary article could not be read in full, so priority remains explicitly qualified; no equivalent count appeared in accessible checked material.
residual_risks: Full manuscript/appendices/source archive of arXiv:2609.02477 could not be inspected. It could contain an unindexed complete five-edge count; no claim of whole-document noncoverage is made.
Earlier computer searches or non-indexed tables of all minimum bondage sets might exist despite negative targeted searches.
The finite certificate and two implementations have only self-review, not external independent validation.

value.rationale: The 2026 counterexample is a canonical finite failure of the planar bondage conjecture. Enumerating every smallest network-link failure pattern and the eight inequivalent geometric configurations gives a complete vulnerability benchmark beyond a mere cardinality threshold or single deletion witness. The object, exact coefficient and orbit spectrum have a direct natural mathematical motivation and the count is not implied by the previously reported minimum.
